methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed phase III RCT with stratified randomization (IGHV, Rai stage), IRC-assessed primary endpoint (PFS), Cox regression with proper CI estimation. Sample size powered for 90% to detect HR 0.41. Sensitivity analyses including crossover censoring strengthen robustness. Subgroup analyses stratified and not multiple-testing adjusted appropriately.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: RCT (1b) comparing noncovalent BTKi to standard chemoimmunotherapy in untreated CLL/SLL. High clinical relevance: pirtobrutinib shows 80% risk reduction for PFS (HR 0.199) and improved safety vs BendaR. Changes treatment landscape for BTKi-naive patients, extends BTKi class beyond covalent inhibitors.

reporting_quality.justification: Excellent CONSORT reporting with flow diagram, baseline characteristics (Table 1), primary and secondary efficacy/safety endpoints clearly defined (Tables 2-3). Exposure-adjusted safety analyses account for treatment duration differences. IRC blinding for primary outcome reduces bias. Comprehensive acknowledgment of limitations.

novelty_literature.justification: First Phase III RCT of noncovalent BTKi (pirtobrutinib) in treatment-naive CLL/SLL. While pirtobrutinib demonstrated efficacy in R/R setting, frontline novel BTKi class represents new evidence. Extends utility beyond cBTKi-resistant patients.

writing_presentation.justification: Excellent organization with clear motivation, comprehensive methods, detailed results with Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by IGHV status (Figure 2). Discussion appropriately contextualizes vs prior BTKi trials and addresses sequencing questions. Limitations section transparent about open-label design and missing OS maturity.

key_strengths: Large effect size for primary endpoint: pirtobrutinib HR 0.199 (80% risk reduction vs BendaR), 24-month PFS 93.4% vs 70.7%
IRC-blinded primary endpoint assessment minimizes bias in open-label design
Superior safety profile: grade ≥3 AE 40% vs 67.4%, dose reductions 3.6% vs 31.1%, discontinuations 4.3% vs 15.2%
Consistent benefit across subgroups including high-risk (TP53 mutations, complex karyotype, unmutated IGHV)
Interim OS analysis favors pirtobrutinib (HR 0.257) despite 52.9% crossover
key_concerns: Excluded del(17p) patients; findings not generalizable to highest-risk subgroup
Open-label design allows potential investigator bias in treatment decisions and follow-up management
Median 28.1-month PFS follow-up may be relatively short for frontline CLL/SLL; median PFS not reached in pirtobrutinib arm
OS remains immature with only 3% mortality; final OS analysis pending
Higher bleeding rates with pirtobrutinib (25.7% vs 1.5%) though mostly low-grade; requires monitoring
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous Phase III RCT demonstrating pirtobrutinib superiority over BendaR for first-line CLL/SLL with large effect size, superior safety, and consistent subgroup benefit. Appropriate for Tier 1: strong novelty (new BTKi class frontline), rigorous design (IRC-blinded), clinical significance (paradigm-shifting). Third positive Phase III pirtobrutinib study.
